description: Curated SecHub Resources SC4S pack for Zeek JSON log records relayed as one JSON object per line, with fixture-backed conn, dns, http, ssl, notice, files, x509, ssh, dhcp, rdp, weird, software, known_hosts, intel, and smtp families.

normalized_fields.zeek_log_type: Fixture/source log family for conn, dns, http, ssl, notice, files, x509, ssh, dhcp, rdp, weird, software, known_hosts, intel, or smtp
normalized_fields.src_ip: Originator/source IP from id.orig_h or notice src
normalized_fields.src_port: Originator/source port from id.orig_p or notice p
normalized_fields.dest_ip: Responder/destination IP from id.resp_h or notice dst
normalized_fields.dest_port: Responder/destination port from id.resp_p or notice p
normalized_fields.action: Zeek conn_state, HTTP method, notice note, or family fallback
normalized_fields.signature: Notice message/note, DNS query, HTTP host, TLS SNI, or connection state triage value
normalized_fields.file_id: Zeek file unique identifier (fuid) for files.log records
normalized_fields.file_name: Filename from Zeek files.log where available
normalized_fields.file_mime_type: MIME type from Zeek file analysis
normalized_fields.file_seen_bytes: Observed bytes from Zeek files.log seen_bytes
normalized_fields.file_total_bytes: Total bytes from Zeek files.log total_bytes where available
normalized_fields.file_md5: MD5 hash from Zeek files.log when configured/emitted
normalized_fields.x509_id: Zeek x509 record identifier / certificate FUID
normalized_fields.x509_not_valid_before: Certificate not-valid-before timestamp from Zeek x509.log
normalized_fields.x509_not_valid_after: Certificate not-valid-after timestamp from Zeek x509.log
normalized_fields.ssh_auth_success: SSH authentication result from Zeek ssh.log
normalized_fields.ssh_client: SSH client/software string from Zeek ssh.log
normalized_fields.ssh_server: SSH server/software string from Zeek ssh.log
normalized_fields.ssh_cipher_alg: SSH cipher algorithm from Zeek ssh.log
normalized_fields.ssh_host_key_alg: SSH host-key algorithm from Zeek ssh.log
normalized_fields.dhcp_client_addr: DHCP client address from Zeek dhcp.log
normalized_fields.dhcp_server_addr: DHCP server address from Zeek dhcp.log
normalized_fields.dhcp_mac: Client hardware/MAC address from Zeek dhcp.log
normalized_fields.dhcp_host_name: Client hostname option from Zeek dhcp.log
normalized_fields.dhcp_assigned_addr: Assigned lease address from Zeek dhcp.log
normalized_fields.dhcp_msg_types: Vector of DHCP message types observed in the transaction
normalized_fields.rdp_cookie: RDP cookie value, often a truncated username, from Zeek rdp.log
normalized_fields.rdp_result: RDP negotiation/GCC result from Zeek rdp.log
normalized_fields.rdp_security_protocol: RDP security protocol chosen by the server
normalized_fields.rdp_client_name: RDP client machine name from Zeek rdp.log
normalized_fields.weird_name: Weird::Info name for unusual/exceptional activity rows
normalized_fields.weird_addl: Additional weird activity context from Zeek Weird::Info addl
normalized_fields.weird_notice: Boolean indicating whether Zeek also emitted the weird as a notice
normalized_fields.weird_source: Analyzer/source string for a weird activity row
normalized_fields.software_host: Host address detected running software from Zeek Software::Info host
normalized_fields.software_port: Port associated with detected server software from host_p
normalized_fields.software_type: Zeek software type enum string where available
normalized_fields.software_name: Detected software name from Zeek Software::Info name
normalized_fields.known_host: Host address logged by Zeek known-hosts policy script
normalized_fields.intel_indicator: Indicator value from Zeek Intel::Info seen.indicator
normalized_fields.intel_indicator_type: Indicator type from Zeek Intel::Info seen.indicator_type
normalized_fields.intel_seen_where: Where Zeek saw the indicator from seen.where
normalized_fields.intel_matched_types: Indicator type set that matched the Intel framework
normalized_fields.intel_sources: Intelligence sources that supplied the matched indicator
normalized_fields.smtp_helo: Zeek SMTP HELO/EHLO string from SMTP::Info. Synthetic-equivalent fixture only; local SMTP logging policy and encryption affect presence.
normalized_fields.smtp_mailfrom: Zeek SMTP envelope sender (`mailfrom`) preserved for mail-flow triage using synthetic example addresses.
normalized_fields.smtp_rcptto: Zeek SMTP recipient list (`rcptto`) preserved as multi-value recipient context.
normalized_fields.smtp_subject: Zeek SMTP message subject field when Zeek extracts it; can be sensitive and must not be dropped/redacted by default without review.
normalized_fields.smtp_last_reply: Zeek SMTP server reply/status text from `last_reply` for delivery/result triage.

timestamp_policy.primary_timezone: UTC Z in fixture ts field
timestamp_policy.notes: Fixtures use ISO-8601 UTC timestamps. Epoch JSON timestamp variants require local confirmation before parser/props expansion.

field_delimiting.notes: Each record is compact Zeek JSON with a synthetic marker/log_type field for fixture validation only.

source.reference: Official Zeek logging/log record documentation and public Zeek source record definitions; parser-ecosystem corroboration from Elastic/Filebeat Zeek module docs only; fixtures are synthetic-equivalent examples shaped to public documentation, including files/x509/ssh source record definitions added in 2026-06-14 hardening, DHCP/RDP source record definitions plus SC4S route correction added in 2026-06-15 hardening, Weird/Software/Known-hosts source records added in 2026-06-16 hardening, and SMTP source/docs evidence from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zeek/zeek/master/scripts/base/protocols/smtp/main.zeek plus https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zeek/zeek-docs/master/logs/smtp.rst.
source.notes: Fixtures use example.test names, RFC5737 documentation IP ranges, synthetic UIDs, and synthetic markers; no customer, PCAP-derived, or production sensor data. SMTP coverage is grounded in the public Zeek SMTP::Info source record and smtp.log documentation.

curation.notes: Selected from 2026-06-13 source-coverage canvas; 2026-06-14 hardening expanded fixture-backed Zeek JSON coverage to files, x509, and ssh; 2026-06-15 hardening added DHCP/RDP fixtures and corrected parser routing for non-uid Zeek families; 2026-06-16 hardening added Weird, Software, and Known-hosts fixture/read-back coverage.

transport.notes: Uppercase transport from native Zeek proto.

signature_id.notes: Zeek connection UID, not a global detection signature.

file_name.notes: File analysis filename where Zeek emits it.

file_hash.notes: File hash fields only when local Zeek configuration emits them.

dhcp_assigned_addr.notes: DHCP lease assignment context, not generic destination identity.

rdp_client_name.notes: RDP client machine context where emitted.

weird_name.notes: Zeek weird activity name where log_type=weird.

known_host.notes: Known-host address inventory context where log_type=known_hosts.

threat_indicator.notes: Zeek Intel framework match context; not complete threat-intel lifecycle validation.

email_sender.notes: SMTP envelope sender from Zeek SMTP::Info; partial email triage only.

email_recipient.notes: SMTP recipient list from Zeek SMTP::Info; partial email triage only.

email_subject.notes: Subject can be sensitive and is preserved by default for review, not validation of message-content collection.

cim.notes: Partial Network Traffic, DNS, Web, TLS, and Intrusion Detection guidance only; not full CIM certification.

finding.title.notes: Weird activity title/additional context; partial finding-style mapping only.

device.name.notes: DHCP hostname or RDP client name context; not a complete asset inventory mapping.

device.ip.notes: Software/known-host address context; not validated asset inventory.

threat_intel.indicator.value.notes: Indicator value seen by Zeek Intel framework.

email.subject.notes: Partial SMTP subject mapping with privacy caveat.

ocsf.notes: OCSF mapping is helper guidance only.

url.path.notes: HTTP URI as emitted by Zeek.

x509.subject.common_name.notes: Certificate subject string; not parsed into CN components.

x509.issuer.common_name.notes: Certificate issuer string; not parsed into CN components.

event.outcome.notes: SSH auth_success can be mapped to outcome by local search knowledge if desired.

host.name.notes: DHCP hostname or RDP client name context where emitted.

related.ip.notes: Related endpoint and lease IP context.

event.reason.notes: Weird activity reason/context and SMTP last-reply/status context; partial field-name guidance only.

observer.ip.notes: Zeek software/known-host observed host IP; partial helper mapping only.

threat.indicator.name.notes: Indicator value from Zeek Intel framework match.

threat.indicator.type.notes: Indicator type from Zeek Intel framework match.

email.subject.notes: Partial SMTP subject mapping with privacy caveat.

ecs.notes: ECS mapping is partial and field-name guidance only.

pack_variants.label: Zeek JSON log relay
pack_variants.description: Zeek JSON records preserving native log family, uid/fuid/id/uids/host identifiers, network tuple, file/certificate/SSH/DHCP/RDP/weird/software/known-hosts/intel context, and family context.
known_limitations: No live Zeek relay replay/read-back captured.
Zeek JSON timestamp style and optional field behavior depend on local LogAscii configuration.

Only conn, dns, http, ssl, notice, files, x509, ssh, dhcp, rdp, weird, software, known_hosts, intel, and smtp families are fixture-backed; additional package-specific/local Zeek logs remain future coverage.

cribl.notes: Use only after sampling the local Zeek JSON feed. Do not drop ts, uid, log family, source/destination tuple, notice/note, DNS query, HTTP host/URI/status, or TLS SNI by default.

vector.notes: Vector support is recorded as a conservative sources/transforms/sinks mapping only: collector/API relay path; keep credential custody and checkpoints outside this pack and preserve source timestamps and raw payloads. No Vector config artifact is generated by this pack yet.

fluent_bit.notes: Fluent Bit support is recorded as a conservative collector/pipeline mapping only: collector/API relay path; keep credential custody and checkpoints outside this pack and preserve source timestamps and raw payloads. No Fluent Bit config artifact is generated by this pack yet.

validation_commands: Start Data Prepper with the generated pipelines.yaml in a disposable test container and confirm pipeline startup before replay/read-back.
data_prepper.notes: Data Prepper support is recorded as a conservative OpenSearch ingestion pipeline mapping only: collector/API relay path; keep credential custody and checkpoints outside this pack and preserve source timestamps and raw payloads. No Data Prepper pipeline artifact is generated by this pack yet.

opensearch_dashboards.notes: OpenSearch Dashboards support is recorded as visualization-target metadata only. Splunk dashboards, where present, have not been automatically translated to OpenSearch saved objects or live-tested.

known_limitations: No live Zeek relay, SC4S runtime replay, or Splunk read-back evidence; keep curated/unverified and do not promote to validated/verified.
Fixtures are synthetic-equivalent examples, not real Zeek sensor records.
Local Zeek version, package scripts, LogAscii JSON timestamp configuration, unset-field behavior, and collector wrappers affect field presence.
Reduction candidates are opt-in and review-required; no default lossy drops are included.
Only conn, DNS, HTTP, SSL/TLS, notice, files, x509, SSH, DHCP, RDP, weird, software, known-hosts, and intel records are fixture-backed; other package-specific/local Zeek logs remain future coverage.

SMTP coverage is synthetic-equivalent from public Zeek SMTP record definitions only; encrypted submission paths, local analyzer policy, message-content privacy handling, and real mail-flow replay/read-back remain unverified.
